Autohome's instrumented 530Li vs E 300 L test measured 263.2 PS on the dyno (above the claimed 258 PS) and 0-100 km/h in 6.18 s, narrowly quicker than the Mercedes.
Autohome rates the 530Li's 100-0 km/h braking (38.89-41.48 m over 10 runs) as only average for its class; the E 300 L stopped shorter without obvious fade.
Autohome reports the 530Li showed body bounce and a sluggish rear in the moose test, noting it has no rear anti-roll bar, and reached 72.5 km/h versus 73.4 km/h for the E 300 L.
In Autohome's stationary-car AEB test the 530Li warned early but could only mitigate the impact at 80 km/h, while the E 300 L stopped fully up to 100 km/h.
In Autohome's child-dummy pedestrian AEB test the 530Li avoided impact up to 70 km/h, which editors call very robust, versus 50 km/h for the E 300 L.
Autohome measured 9.19 L/100 km in mixed driving for the 530Li versus 9.61 L/100 km for the E 300 L, noting both trail hybrids.

rationale: Beijing Benz long-wheelbase E-Class, the direct China-only rival to the 5 Series Li: same 2.0T 48V mild-hybrid 258 hp class, owners cross-shop it with the 530Li, and Autohome tests the two head to head.
